Equating coordinates gives 2k+l=-1 and 3k-l=6. Thus k=1, l=-3, and k+l=-2.
For x^2/5-y^2/4=1, the foci are at ±3 on the x-axis. With Q=(-a,-b), quadrilateral F'QFP is a parallelogram of area 6b, so b=4. Substitution gives a^2/5-16/4=1, hence a=5 in quadrant I.
At parameter a, slope is 3a^2+2a. The y-intercept is g(a)=a^3+a^2-(3a^2+2a)(a+1)=-2a^3-4a^2-2a. The limit is g'(1)/2=-16/2=-8.
For unit-speed angular parameterization (cos t,sin t), velocity=(-sin t,cos t) and acceleration=(-cos t,-sin t); their dot product is 0.
Let c be focal distance. The triangle-area ratio is a/c=2. The focal triangle perimeter is 2a+2c=6, so c=1,a=2; b^2=a^2-c^2=3 and a^2+b^2=7.

At P(a,b), tangent slope is na/b. Passing through (-2,0) gives b=(na/b)(a+2). Together with b^2=n(a^2+1), this yields a=1, b=sqrt(2n), and a_n=sqrt(n/2). Then 1/(a_n+a_{n+1})=sqrt(2)(sqrt(n+1)-sqrt(n)); summing n=1..80 gives 8sqrt(2).

Re-evaluation: extrema of sqrt(x^2+y^2) on this ellipse occur at x=±1,y=0 (minimum radius 1) and x=0,y=±2 (maximum radius 2), so sum=3.

The line is y=p(x-p), so x=p+y/p. Substitution into y^2=4px gives y^2-4y-4p^2=0; the two y-values differ by 4sqrt(1+p^2). The line's length factor per unit y-difference is sqrt(1+p^2), yielding 4(p^2+1).
The area is S=x^3/3, so dS/dt=x^2 dx/dt=2. At x=2, dx/dt=1/2 and dy/dt=2x dx/dt=2. Speed is sqrt(1/4+4)=sqrt(17)/2.
Let |OA|=u, |OB|=v; they are perpendicular and u^2+v^2=36. The two conditions give OP·OA=u^2/2 and OP·OB=v^2/2, so OP=(OA+OB)/2. Then BP=(OA-OB)/2 and |BP|=sqrt(u^2+v^2)/2=3.
